findings.title: include_website_name missing '?' breaks ActiveModelSerializers convention
findings.body: The predicate method is defined as `include_website_name` instead of `include_website_name?`. AMS conventions require a trailing `?` for conditional attribute inclusion methods (as seen with all other include_* methods, e.g. `include_email?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). Without the `?`, AMS will not recognize this method as the inclusion guard for `website_name`, so the attribute will likely always be serialized (or behave inconsistently) regardless of whether `website` is present, defeating the purpose of this check and potentially leaking an unwanted empty/nil website_name attribute.

findings.title: website_name not covered by untrusted_attributes guard
findings.body: `untrusted_attributes` lists `:website` but not `:website_name`. Since website_name is derived from website and may contain more revealing info (the full path), TL0 users viewed anonymously will still have website_name present in the serialized output even though website itself is hidden, inconsistent with the intent of the untrusted_attributes restriction and the first spec in the test file which doesn't check for website_name.

findings.title: Fragile domain-matching heuristic for website_name
findings.body: The logic in website_name uses split('.').length comparisons and ends_with? checks to decide whether website and instance share a domain. This can produce incorrect results for cases like 'notexample.com' matching 'example.com' via ends_with?("." + host) only partially guards against false positives, but subdomain-length-based matching (elsif branch) can mismatch for domains with different numbers of labels (e.g., co.uk-style TLDs), producing wrong website_name values silently rather than erring safely to just the host name.
